speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
text: Can the Minister provide an update on what the minimum viable product would look like at the launch of Healthier SG, and a roadmap for subsequent releases?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: In recent years, Singapore has been making significant efforts to address this.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: Conversations around mental health have become much easier among Singaporeans over the years, and this is not a coincidence.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: It is made possible by the efforts from the Government, ground-up groups and community partners, like Calm Collective, Total Wellness Initiative, Silver Ribbon, to name a few, to destigmatise mental health issues.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: Last year, the PAP launched the #bettertogether campaign to support these efforts further.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: These efforts have been particularly important in today's world, notwithstanding the impact of COVID-19, depression, anxiety and other mental health issues that are ever-present.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: I believe this is a step in the right direction and like many mental health advocates, I look forward to the details of the plans.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: Therefore, may I ask the Minister, what are the updates from the Interagency Task Force on Mental Health and Well-being?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: While mothers are often primary caregivers in a child's life, fathers are also critical in providing support, love and stability for the family and children.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: Research has shown that fathers who are involved in their children's lives can often have a positive impact on their mental health and well-being.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: For mothers, fathers who are there can provide emotional and practical support during pregnancy, childbirth and the postpartum period.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: Research has also shown that fathers can be indirectly impacted from depression.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: Could the Ministry update on its plans for the Interagency Task Force on Mental Health and Well-being in the year ahead?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: But vaping appears to be growing in popularity with young people.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: There are reports of primary school pupils getting caught as well.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: Some people think that vaping is healthier than smoking.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: A Johns Hopkins' report suggests that vaping is not safe, may be bad for the heart and lungs and may be just as addictive as cigarettes.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: The fun, fruity "flavours" of these e-vaporisers adds to the misconception that vapes are harmless.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: I am worried that a new generation is getting hooked on nicotine.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: Thus, I would like to suggest HSA consider working with other agencies to educate youths and the general public that vaping is not harmless and that vaping is illegal.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: I also hope HSA could work with schools and other law enforcement agencies to double these enforcement efforts.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: I suggest MOH consider doubling the fine quantum and consider a jail sentence for repeat offenders.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: However, with the move to online and mobile enrolment into these programmes, can the Ministry share how it plans to ensure continued, easy access to these programmes for seniors who may not be digitally-savvy.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This is higher than the base rate which we used in 2019, which is 525 per 100,000 person years.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Nevertheless, due to the concerted effort of Singaporeans, we remain one of the countries with the lowest mortality rate and excess death rate in the world throughout the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Dr Tan also asked about strengthening our vaccine capability.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This is something we are actively looking at, both in terms of building up our research and development (R&D) capabilities and also anchoring local manufacturing capabilities here.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I will give a fuller update at a subsequent Sitting, because we are going to table our full After-Action Review in the House.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This will take place not too long after the COS debate.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: A major after-effect of the COVID-19 pandemic is that it inspired us to accelerate the changes to our healthcare system.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: As a result, the healthcare system is now at a very decisive stage of a major transformation, working off a foundation that took many, many years to build.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: And now, we look at the healthcare system not as one system, but as three interlinked systems.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: First, the acute care system, which is mature, well-developed.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This is a system comprising of hospitals, specialist clinics, treating the sick.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I would say this is a teenager or adolescent.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We are putting more emphasis on this through preventive care, through Healthier SG.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We need aged care to take place predominantly in the community and not at nursing homes.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The imperative for this transformation is our rapidly ageing population, which I think is the biggest social development for this generation.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The impetus to act now is COVID-19, which made things that were hitherto impossible now possible.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Most importantly, through the crisis, the crisis brought to the forefront the power of preventive care, like good hygiene, screening tests and vaccinations.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Mr Chairman, today, I will give the House an update on the three systems and answer questions at the same time.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But before that, there are a few common, foundational issues undergirding all three healthcare systems, which my colleagues in MOH will address.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: First, we need the right size and quality of manpower.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Senior Parliamentary Secretary Rahayu will be speaking on this.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I have explained in the House before, that with a rising population of seniors who will fall sick more often and the shrinking population of new local entrants into the workforce, the numbers simply do not add up.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will not have enough local healthcare workers to support our healthcare needs.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We have to do first whatever we can to develop our local pipeline of talent, including some of the suggestions that Mr Gerald Giam has put forward – attract retired nurses to return; serve as locums; increase male participation, that will be most welcome.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But we still need to complement it with foreign healthcare workers, from varied sources.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Various Members raised the issue about the welfare of workers.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But fundamentally, the best safeguard for their welfare is to have sufficient manpower.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Insufficient manpower and you have people who are so responsible, they are going to burn their weekends, they are going to burn their rest days and so on.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: You have to simply beef up the manpower resources.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Senior Parliamentary Secretary Rahayu will speak more about it.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: As for foreign healthcare workers who become valuable members of our team and demonstrate commitment to Singapore, we should be prepared to integrate them into our society, just as we do for many foreign professionals.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: At the same time, and a few Members have raised this, society needs to appreciate and respect healthcare workers.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The great majority of our patients, and their loved ones and their family members, do.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will need to take a firmer stand against this.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We need, as Mr Ang Wei Neng suggested, a consistent understanding across the healthcare system on what constitutes abuse of healthcare workers.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We need to then empower hospitals to take a firmer stand against such abuse.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: When hospitals take such a firm stand against abuse, the hospitals must feel confident that their management, MOH, the Minister and hopefully, this House and the public, will stand behind in protecting our healthcare workers against abuse.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: MOH has convened a workgroup to study this issue.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will be sharing the findings on MOH's plans later this month.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The second undergirding issue is we need the right IT systems and tools, to allow patients' key health data to be collected and shared across health providers safely and securely, to ensure seamless and integrated care.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Senior Minister of State Janil Puthucheary will elaborate on this.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Tan Tock Seng Hospital Integrated Care Hub (TTSH-ICH) will also start operations this year.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Preparation works for the redevelopment of Alexandra Hospital and the new Eastern Integrated Health Campus are also in progress.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: While not part of the acute care system, polyclinics are a very important part of our healthcare ecosystem.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The Sembawang Polyclinic will start operations in the second half of this year, and so too the Tampines North Polyclinic.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Another eight will come on stream by 2030.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But we should not overbuild or worse, think that the solution to future challenges of healthcare lies only in infrastructure and the number of beds.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Ultimately, with an ageing population, we need to become healthier.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: And this brings us to the second system, which is the population health system.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We are building it up through Healthier SG.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Dr Tan Wu Meng, Dr Lim Wee Kiak, Mr Ang Wei Neng, Ms Ng Ling Ling and probably a couple more others, have asked for updates on Healthier SG.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We want each of our residents to enrol with a family doctor, to build a long-term patient-doctor relationship.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We think the doctor is best placed to guide a resident to better health.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: That makes family doctors the lynchpin of Healthier SG, the most important component.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Therefore, we have been engaging our private sector GPs to co-develop Healthier SG.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We are supporting GPs in many ways: IT grants, annual service fees for Healthier SG when they take care of enrolled participants.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This is a new stream of revenue for the GPs, for managing the health of enrolled residents.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will also be fully funding preventive services, like nationally recommended vaccinations and health screenings for enrolled Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: GPs will very likely have to deliver more of such services, which is another source of revenue.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We have been explaining to GPs that with greater investment in preventive care, the primary care will grow, both in terms of size and importance.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But GPs will incur more costs, but they will also earn more fee-based income and services-based incomes from the Government.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It is voluntary for GPs to be a Healthier SG clinic.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We have about 1,600 GP clinics in Singapore focused on primary care.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Our assessment is that the great majority appreciates the objective of Healthier SG.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They think it is a move that should have come earlier and they want to be part of it.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But the sums have to work for them and we are working with them closely.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I also announced that we will launch a pre-enrolment exercise in May 2023.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Those aged 40 and above, already have chronic illnesses and regularly visit their GPs.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But their GPs need to sign up for Healthier SG.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: If they have not signed up, please try to persuade your GPs to sign up.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This will ensure that this group of patients who need Healthier SG the most do not get crowded out.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Mr Ang Wei Neng suggested using health carnivals to encourage sign-ups and volunteered the Pioneer Division to be the first.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We are keen to take it up and will discuss with you as well.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: You are, indeed, the pioneer and many more community and grassroots organisations will come after you.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This includes, one, a first Healthier SG doctor consultation which will be fully subsidised by the Government.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Two, once the first consultation is completed, you will be awarded 3,000 Healthpoints worth $20.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: To earn 3,000 Healthpoints using Healthy 365, you must walk 5,000 steps for 300 days.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This is MOH's way of saying, "Well done!

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Welcome to Healthier SG." Three, nationally recommended health screenings and vaccinations, like influenza and mammograms will be free of charge for eligible residents.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Four, after seeing the doctor, you want to heed his advice and to be more physically active, our community organisations will be organising more activities near your home.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Dr Tan Wu Meng talked about sessions being terminated.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: There was a time when we were cost-conscious and wanted to be cost-effective.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Because of Healthier SG, we want to provide stronger support.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, even for those with a lower participation rate, we want to work with the local community, beef up participation and give sufficient lead time for us to be able to do that.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But what has been suspended, I am afraid we cannot undo.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, please erase that from your memory and let us look forward.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Ultimately, the best payback is better health for everyone.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This includes, one, enhanced subsidies for chronic drugs at GP clinics.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Today, CHAS already provides significant subsidies for patients with low chronic medication needs.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Just with their CHAS subsidies, they pay $0 or very little for their visits and medications.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: However, there are patients with complex chronic diseases who need several drugs and medication.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The current CHAS benefits are not enough for them.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Hence, these patients tend to go to polyclinics to get their subsidised drugs.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They will be available at your enrolled Healthier SG GP clinic.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I should emphasise that this Healthier SG CHAS Chronic Tier is an option for this group of patients.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It is an option because we know that some of these patients in this group are used to certain brands of drugs and they prefer to get it from their GPs even though the drugs are not subsidised.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, now, we make the subsidised and cheaper alternatives used by polyclinics available to these patients through their private GP clinics, but they are not compelled to switch.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They can stay with the unsubsidised drugs that they are used to if they wish to.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Patients can use MediSave to pay their bills fully, up to the withdrawal limit.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We are working closely with TCM practitioners by providing more support on R&D to generate evidence on the efficacies of TCM.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: There will be more developments in this area, which I will update the House when ready.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Nursing homes have, indeed, provided important support to many families with frail parents.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It is highly subsidised and supports families who are no longer able to take care of their loved ones at home.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: However, building more nursing homes is not a sustainable long-term solution.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We run the risk of becoming over-reliant on it.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Because the worst enemy of the aged is often not diseases, but isolation and loneliness.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Without the companionship and love of family members or friends, the loss of function will hasten and they become frail very quickly.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: As I mentioned in this House before, research shows that the impact of loneliness on an elderly is equivalent to smoking 15 cigarettes a day.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Our seniors need friends, relationships, love and activities around them.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They need to feel active and purposeful, doing full-time work, part-time work, volunteer work, take walks in the park, hear the laughter of children, occasionally get into a squabble with their kakis – all these keep them healthy.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: These things can even reverse frailty in certain instances, but they can happen only if the seniors can age actively in the community.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The Ministry of National Development (MND) has announced that they are building more Community Care Apartments.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But it will not cater to the great majority.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Therefore, what is more important is for seniors to be able to age in their current homes, which hold unique memories.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: To do so, we can leverage two important assets.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They are designed with many common spaces for interaction amongst residents – void decks, exercise corners, coffee shops, supermarkets, hawker centres.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They served a different imperative in the early years of our nation building, but now, these common spaces offer opportunities for seniors to age healthily in the community.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Second, our community partners, who have been providing social care and support in our housing estates.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They have built up very precious personal relationships with residents.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We have been working with them to implement pilot programmes for ageing in communities.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Recently, I visited Montfort Care's AAC at Marine Parade.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They told me there are 5,000 seniors in the area they are in charge of and they have so far identified 400 seniors living alone.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: These 400 are their top priority for engagement.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, like MOH, they know from experience, the pain and detriment of loneliness.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Like many AAC partners I have visited, Montfort came to the conclusion as everybody on how best to attract seniors – it is to makan together.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, once or twice a week, they get donors to donate food, and volunteers to prepare the food, serve it in a nice environment like a nicely done up void deck, and seniors will come and gather.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Then, they start to watch out for one another.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The centre's staff can then further engage them to ensure that they are taking their medication, they are going to their health screenings, and they can monitor their health.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I did not know that until I visited many of them, especially now that we have many Gym Tonics on the ground.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Many seniors who do not like to leave their homes will go to the gym.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Many seniors who do not like to leave their homes will come to the gym.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I suspect they heard enough stories of how gym work actually strengthens them and people who were immobile are able to walk again and even reverse frailty in certain circumstances.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We are putting these ground experiences together into an effective and workable operating model for all AACs, even as we expand the network.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: To do this well, our community partners will need stronger support in both money and manpower.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We are racing against time because the pace of ageing in Singapore is relentless.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But if done well, this will be one of the best gifts to our seniors.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Mr Chairman, over the years, MOH has been explaining the need to shift healthcare from hospitals to the community.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: With the three healthcare systems, we are making this into a concrete reality.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But if care is shifting from hospitals to community, so must the other aspects of healthcare.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We cannot just have standards and rules for hospitals and clinics.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They need to flow across different healthcare providers and settings.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: That is why we will be presenting the Health Information Bill to improve the current situation of data collection and sharing.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Likewise, the same argument can be made for healthcare financing for patients.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The healthcare financing framework, which is "S+3Ms", namely, subsidies, MediShield Life, MediSave and MediFund – they must extend beyond hospitals to wherever healthcare services are delivered.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We are, therefore, undertaking a review of our healthcare financing framework to make it more premises-neutral.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In the meantime, we will make three smaller, no-regrets moves.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Dr Tan Wu Meng has told the story of Ah Ma twice – once during the White Paper on Healthier SG and once just a couple of hours ago.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: As a start, this will apply to 25 home medical and home nursing providers that are receiving subvention and support from MOH.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: When the scheme stabilises, we will consider extending to the rest of the service providers.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Dr Tan Wu Meng also suggested allowing patients to take their blood tests at polyclinics before their surgery and to standardise their forms.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will look into that, but we are mindful not to add further workload to the polyclinics, especially with Healthier SG coming onstream and they are extremely busy.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The second thing we will do is normalise telehealth for care delivery.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: During the COVID-19 pandemic, we wanted healthy individuals to recover from COVID-19 infections at home, so as to minimise their visits to the clinics.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Infected persons isolated at home, they could seek consultation from a doctor online and have medication sent to them.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Doctors too, can now leverage technology to attend and care for more patients.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: To support and encourage the use of telehealth during the pandemic, we extended usage of MediSave and CHAS Chronic subsidies for teleconsultations for chronic disease management.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Hence, we have decided to continue the pandemic arrangement and normalise the use of appropriate telehealth and make it part of routine chronic disease management.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng and Mr Xie Yao Quan have asked about this.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Survey findings consistently show that the great majority of Singaporeans prefer to pass on at home, in familiar surroundings, in the presence of loved ones, instead of an unfamiliar hospital surrounding.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: However, currently three in five deaths still happen in hospitals.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We have a long way to go in fulfilling the wishes of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Hence, we are improving the clinical protocols in the hospitals.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We are upskilling providers to develop general palliative care capabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We are engaging in early conversations with patients and their loved ones on their wishes.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Later this year, MOH will be embarking on an outreach effort, to encourage more Singaporeans to plan ahead with a Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA) and Advance Care Plan (ACP).

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But we also need to work on expanding the capacity of the palliative care sector.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Community palliative care providers – namely HCA, Assisi, Dover Park – they have been doing a tremendous job.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They provide three modes of palliative care – at home, in day hospice or in the inpatient hospice.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They have also been raising significant amount of charity dollars every year to complement Government funding to support their operations.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: To unlock their capacity constraints, hospices will need additional resources.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will grant them more resources through a new bundled-per-patient funding rate and we will learn from the pilot, review the arrangements, with a view to mainstream the scheme next year.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Healthcare inflation in 2021 is 1.1%, 2022 is 2.2%, and this is calculated post-subsidies and significantly lower than general inflation in both years.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will continue to keep healthcare costs affordable through our S+3Ms framework.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Low-income Singaporeans, in particular, can be assured that additional financial assistance will be available to you, if you need them.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This is a question raised by Mr Xie Yao Quan.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will extend financial assistance on a case-by-case basis to needy PRs, especially those with a strong nexus to Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: However, for the great majority of Singaporeans who are healthy, the best way to keep healthcare costs low is to stay healthy.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This is another reason why Healthier SG and ageing in communities are the two top priorities now.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: (In Mandarin):   I believe all of us have noticed that Singapore's population is ageing rapidly.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: There are more and more seniors in our neighbourhood.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The burden on the society, family, healthcare system and our national finances will become heavier as well.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Population ageing is an inevitable trend, but this does not mean that our hands are tied or that we have to give in.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We cannot reverse the demographic change but we can change our views towards age.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Many seniors who are above 65 may be old in age, but are young at heart.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Recently, I met an auntie when I was doing a walk-about in my constituency.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: She said to me amicably, "Minister Ong, you are so young.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I am almost 90 but you are only 60 plus.” I replied, "Auntie, actually I am only 53!" Auntie said, without a trace of embarrassment: "Uh, nowadays whether you are in your 50s or 60s, you all look the same!" I thought about it later.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In my memory, he looked haggard and old.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But now, many uncles and aunties in their 60s are still very active and do not look any older than me.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: As the quality of life improves, the life expectancy of Singaporeans has been increasing as well.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The best response is to take care of your health.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: If you can do this, you can refuse to admit that you are old.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Staying healthy is our own responsibility, but the Government will also have policies to take care of the elderly.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: First, MOH is working on the Healthier SG programme, which will be launched soon.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They can choose a family doctor to be their long-term health partner.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: MOH will work with community centres and grassroots organisations to help with the enrolment.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Second, we will try our best to let our seniors to age in the community that they are familiar with.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: As we enter the golden years, the biggest fear is not diseases, but loneliness and isolation.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Once the seniors lose the companionship, care and love of their friends and family, their health will deteriorate and their bodies will become frail.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Ageing in place – with the companionship of family members, neighbours, friends and community volunteers – seniors can stay healthy or even reverse their frailness.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This is an attainable vision, but not one that can be achieved by MOH alone.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Fortunately, we have many community partners that provide care services in our housing estates and build precious relationships with the residents.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Recently, I visited a cafe in Marine Parade.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It is called "独一无二" because the cafe is located at the void deck of block 52.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The volunteers who help out in the centre are seniors themselves.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They go to the centre for one or two days a week and prepare some food to serve the seniors living nearby.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They work together – some cut meat, some clean beansprouts, some do the cooking and some do the plating.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Once they eat together, they start to make friends and become good neighbours.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Afterwards, they start to take care of one another and watch out for one another's health.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The operation of a place like "独一无二" relies on donations from kind-hearted donors.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The Government will consider how to fund such programmes, so that they can spread across the whole island.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Third, we will make changes to the MediSave policy.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Currently, some senior Singaporeans who are wheelchair-bound or bedridden have to seek home medical care.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But under the current policy, MediSave cannot be used for home medical care.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The fourth point is more sensitive, which is end-of-life arrangement or hospice care.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They think it is inauspicious and see it as taboo.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But surveys conducted in recent years show that many Singaporeans prefer to pass on at home, in the company of their loved ones.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In order to fulfil the wishes of Singaporeans in this area, we need to work harder.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Next, we will work together with palliative care provider Dover Park Hospice and their close partner, TTSH, to conduct a pilot programme.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Under the pilot, we will provide more grants and subsidies.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: To encourage these operators to expand their services, we will also allow them to determine the type of palliative care to deliver to the patients based on their care needs, as well as the family circumstances.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I hope that the Government, businesses, community and the people can work together to reform our healthcare system, change our views towards ageing and to help our seniors to enjoy a fulfilling, happy and peaceful golden age.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: (In English): Mr Chairman, let me conclude by addressing Mr Henry Kwek's question on longevity science.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The Geriatric Education and Research Institute and the Centre for Healthy Longevity as well as other similar centres, they are doing very good work.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In the transformation of healthcare, we are dealing with much broader and much more fundamental questions.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I think the definition of medical science lies on a spectrum.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: At one end, medicine is a frontier science.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: As a matter of life and death, it attracts a lot of R&D, including very exciting work on human longevity.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Some of the advances sounds like science fiction.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Today, you can 3D print body replacement parts, you can teach yourselves to fight a disease, you can edit genes to treat cancer.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But we need to exercise caution when translating medicine as a frontier science, no matter how promising and exciting, into public health policy.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We have to ensure that standard clinical practices and healthcare policies do not run ahead of the evidence of clinical benefit and cost-effectiveness.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: And that is one end of medical science.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In the broad middle, medicine is a biological science.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This is where medicine finds wide applications in the treatment of diseases.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It is the heartbeat of our acute care system.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It has improved lives all over the world.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: When people unfortunately fall sick, hospitals do their best to treat them.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Safety nets are set up to try to make healthcare costs affordable.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But make no mistake, we do not like sickness and all countries in the world hope that demand for medical care is as low as possible.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Then, there is the other end of the spectrum.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Here, medicine comprises of relatively simple and general interventions that apply to entire populations – adequate sleep, eat healthily, exercise regularly, do not smoke, do not doctor-hop, go for periodic screenings and vaccinations.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Unlike medicine in hospitals where we wish for less, we want more of such socially good medicine that enhances health, well-being and productivity.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: As Rudolf Virchow, the father of modern pathology and social medicine famously said in 1848, "medicine is a social science, and politics (is)…medicine at a larger scale".

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But this is, of course, back in 1848.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: However, while the benefits are significant in this spectrum, many people are unable to bring themselves to do these simple things that make us healthier.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Because eating well, exercise and so on takes effort, sacrifice, perseverance, the rewards happen gradually and later, and they deny the all-too-human need for instant gratification.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Hence, our public policies need to recognise the positive externalities of this spectrum of medicine and overcome and compensate for this hesitancy in order to maximise social good.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We cannot sweat those minority of abuse cases and let them dictate the overall design of our preventive care system, just like how we design the vaccination system during the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We need to mobilise the support of communities and partners to deliver preventive care well, similar to how we say it takes a village to raise our children.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We need every individual to play a part in health and assume personal responsibility, just like national defence.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It is a new realm of thinking in healthcare policy, but the considerations are not at all unfamiliar in public policy-making.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Mr Chairman, our healthcare system has always reflected the face of Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In the 1960s, we had a lean, cost-efficient system suited to a mainly young and vigorous people.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Today, we have, through the crisis of COVID-19 and all that we, as a nation, have learnt in overcoming it, a powerful impetus to act – decisively, with resolve and extraordinary will, to see us through this necessary transformation.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: And if it is true that politics is medicine on a larger scale, we in this House have the duty to ensure that we, our families and fellow Singaporeans will enjoy good health for generations to come.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Chairman, I thank Members for their suggestions on ways we can enable Singaporeans to keep healthy and build strong families.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Health, like education and housing, is foundational to the well-being of a family.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: When families are healthy, they can thrive, support their seniors and enable their children to flourish and reach their fullest potential in life.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This is why over the years; we have strengthened our policies to build strong and healthy families.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: MOH has been building an integrated ecosystem to support children and their families across the health and social domains.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We are further enhancing it through the Child and Maternal Health and Well-being Strategy.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We have begun the effort to enable families to access cross-domain services at a one-stop community node near their homes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Since November last year, families with young children living in the East have been able to access health services and parenting programmes close to home at FamNex@OTH.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Over the next few months, a wider spectrum of services and programmes for families will be added on with more partnerships forged, providing holistic support for families.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For example, the father can bring his elder child to the library for reading programmes while waiting for the mother and their newborn child who are receiving support on recommended childhood developmental screening and lactation support from Family Nexus.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The family could attend parenting programmes organised by Family Nexus before enjoying a meal at OTH or participate in family-oriented sports activities by ActiveSG.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: One such family who has benefitted from the Family Nexus' support is Mdm D and her family who reside in Tampines.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The FamNex@OTH team noticed that her children frequently hang out at the community space.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: With the help of the volunteer from the Family Service Centre (FSC), Mdm D was connected to the FamNex team from SingHealth and shared her concerns on the health conditions of her children, including her observation that one of her children might be slower in development.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The FamNex community nurses followed up with a comprehensive health assessment for her children with the support of a paediatric nurse from KK Women's and Children's Hospital (KKH) and provided Mdm D with guidance and know-how to better care for her children's health conditions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This includes educating her on the right medication to manage asthma for one of her children, working out a plan to support her child's development and equipping Mdm D with educational resources and visual aids to guide her in monitoring her child's behaviour and symptoms.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: With the support from FamNex@OTH and other partners, Mdm D is now more confident and equipped to care for her children aged two to 18 years.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Chairman, we will also continue to roll out mother-child dyad services at our polyclinics nationwide, enabling more children and mothers to benefit from services such as vaccination, childhood development screenings, breastfeeding and lactation support and maternal mental health screening.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Parents and children can receive support concurrently at a single session without making multiple trips.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We are investing more in upstream measures to help families keep healthy.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This is in line with the Healthier SG effort on preventive health.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: To improve the health outcomes of our women and children, we are going upstream, starting from as early as at the pre-conception stage, ensuring that couples are supported throughout the different stages of their parenthood journey.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In addition, to ensure that we address emerging issues and trends in a relevant manner, we need to adopt an evidence-based approach and be informed by research.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Findings from local studies, such as the Growing Up in Singapore Towards Healthy Outcomes (GUSTO) have shown that maternal depression and anxiety affects the brain development of the foetus, which could give rise to vulnerability, to mood and anxiety disorders in the child's later life as well as their readiness for school.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I am glad that hospitals and professionals are tapping into this evidence-based finding in designing services and resources.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Last month, KKH together with the College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists Singapore launched the Perinatal Mental Health Guidelines.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: These guidelines provide comprehensive advice to better address maternal depression and anxiety during the preconception, antenatal and postnatal phases.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: These guidelines are readable and I encourage all, from family physicians, general practitioners to social workers and couples themselves, to reference them.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Early detection of diseases is key to enable timely intervention to achieve good health outcomes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Which is why we have encouraged our residents to take up the appropriate health screening programmes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Under this programme, all pregnant women receiving outpatient obstetric care at the hospital can access universal antenatal mental health screening and will be referred to the necessary care if they have depressive symptoms.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Through these efforts, families will be supported in keeping healthy through the various chapters of their lives.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We will empower parents, providing them with more evidence-based resources and practical help to raise healthy and happy children.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Our children today grow up in a world of digital services.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: However, the best practices on the use of such devices are not always clear.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I can understand that many parents would be concerned to learn that studies, such as GUSTO, show that early passive screen use for young children, especially those under 18 months old, has been associated with poorer language skills and shorter attention spans when the children are in primary school.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The advisory has been developed by an expert panel comprising professionals from healthcare, social and educational sectors.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: It provides useful tips such as for parents to be role models for positive screen-use behaviours and set boundaries on screen use with children.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We hope that it will be a helpful guide for parents, educators and more.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We share the same view as Dr Wan Rizal that we need to do more to support fathers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The role that fathers play in early childhood development may not be well-known, but it is no less important.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Studies, such as SG LEADS, show that fathers play a sizeable role in the development of a child's self-regulation and ability to delay enjoyment.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This refers to the ability to defer short-term enjoyment for longer-term gain, an important predictor of ability and academic achievement.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Besides parents, we will also leverage existing natural touchpoints, such as schools and preschools, to do more, to give every child a good head start in keeping healthy.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We will be enhancing school health and preschool health programmes, to provide a more comprehensive and holistic school health package for students to foster good healthy habits from young.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: More details will be announced together with the Ministry of Education (MOE) and the Ministry for Social and Family Development (MSF) later this year.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Ultimately, we want to empower families to take charge of their health and enable families to flourish.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We recognise that some families may need more support.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For such families, a single health event can be destabilising.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Early detection and intervention will prevent small issues from snowballing into larger problems later.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Keeping families on an even keel and helping them achieve stability, self-reliance and, ultimately, social mobility.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I agree with Mr Xie Yao Quan that we can do more to integrate health and social services to provide more holistic support for lower-income families.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Today, public healthcare institutions are in partnerships with Social Service Offices (SSOs) to jointly support lower-income residents in their region.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For example, Changi General Hospital (CGH) community care staff and SSO officers work together as one team at SSO@Bedok.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: When families come to SSO@Bedok for financial assistance, CGH community nurses take the opportunity to assess their health needs and provide support, such as advice on recommended health screenings.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Clients with health concerns are referred to the community nurses who are stationed onsite at SSO@Bedok and who will liaise with their primary care doctor if there is a need.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For those who are unable to make a trip down to the SSO, the community nurses visit them at home, together with the SSO officers, to offer support and help.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We are also improving lower-income families' access to health promotion programmes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This involves redesigning the care model and services around these families, facilitating health and developmental screenings, equipping preschools and social agencies to identify and refer at-risk preschool children for further assessment, equipping parents through home visits and fast-tracking referrals for medical appointments where needed.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: These efforts will build on the efforts of existing programmes, like KidSTART and ComLink.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: NUH will partner Care Corner and PAP Community Foundation (PCF) Sparkletots preschools in the West.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: These pilots will provide deeper insights on how we could further strengthen cross-domain collaborations to better support lower-income families.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: If they are proven effective, we will explore scaling them nation-wide to benefit even more families.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: With Healthier SG, we expect these collaborations to be further deepened, particularly with polyclinics and the Primary Care Networks.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Last but not least, we are also enhancing support for caregivers who are the cornerstones of our families' well-being.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Like Mr Gerald Giam and Ms Carrie Tan, we recognise that caregivers play a significant role and must be supported well.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The Government has enhanced our support for caregiving for families over the years.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Last year, we shared more initiatives to recognise caregivers' contributions and ease their burden when we debated the White Paper on Singapore Women's Development.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: MOH has recently enhanced the HCG to further defray the costs of caring for seniors and those with disabilities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This already covers households earning up to the median income per household member.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: As Minister Ong shared earlier, we are also taking steps to further improve affordability for those receiving care at home, as part of the holistic shift for healthcare services to be more premises-neutral and care-centric.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For those taking care of very frail seniors, there are around 60 nursing homes which offer residential respite care.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Others could tap on various subsidised eldercare services, such as home and day care services for respite.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This will offer an additional option for families.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: More details will be shared by MOM at a later time.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: There have also been suggestions to enhance family care leave.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Beyond legislating leave provisions, it is more critical and sustainable for caregivers to be provided with family-friendly work environment, to help them balance work and caregiving responsibilities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We will continue to enhance efforts to support a more family-friendly work culture, including promoting FWAs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We are also enhancing support to PwDs and their caregivers in building an inclusive Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We will share more about our plans later during MSF's COS.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In closing, healthy families lay a foundation for a strong society.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We want to empower families to sustain their health through the chapters of their lives – making it easier for them to access services and enhancing support for caregivers; adopting a preventive health approach to better support fathers, mothers and their children; maximising their well-being and helping their children achieve their fullest potential in life and creating a Singapore that is truly made for families.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I suspend the Sitting and will take the Chair at 4.00 pm.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Sitting accordingly suspended  at 3.38 pm until 4.00 pm.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Chairman, Sir, as our healthcare system evolves, services such as home care and teleconsultations are becoming more commonplace.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These changes drove our move towards a premises-neutral and services-based regulatory regime.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Patients need to remember and repeat their medical history and there is an administrative burden on providers to avoid unnecessary investigations or tests.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Some programmes are attempting to close this gap, like the Primary Tech-Enhanced Care-Hypertension (PTEC-HT) Programme in polyclinics mentioned last year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This allows patients to submit their blood pressure data to their primary care team who views these readings through a dashboard.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: A patient can change polyclinics and the new polyclinic can continue to monitor the patient's blood pressure through the dashboard.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The patient need not record and repeat their blood pressure readings from the original polyclinic.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These are small steps in the right direction and we need to build on these steps.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It is critical that healthcare providers can collect, access and share standardised health information across settings, to facilitate the provision of uninterrupted and holistic care.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: For example, we screen women at risk of gestational diabetes during pregnancy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We know that early detection and intervention for such women can improve both maternal and infant health outcomes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: With Healthier SG and data sharing, GPs can identify women with pre-diabetes and support them on lifestyle changes to prevent the onset of diabetes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: When the woman becomes pregnant, data sharing will enable her health information to be accessed by her obstetrician, who will then know about her higher risk to develop gestational diabetes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: If she does develop the condition during pregnancy, she will have a higher risk of developing diabetes within the five next years after delivery.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: So, her regular GP will need to know about what happened during the pregnancy and so work with her on preventive measures to keep diabetes at bay.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Data sharing enables care and preventive care provision to take place seamlessly as she goes through different stages of her life and this data sharing needs to happen from the community practitioners to the hospital specialists, and back again.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: I agree with Dr Lim Wee Kiak that data sharing is needed to enhance patient care and on the need to expand the NEHR, as with Ms Mariam Jaafar on building our capabilities to harness the power of digital tools.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The NEHR was designed to facilitate data sharing for care coordination and give healthcare providers greater visibility of the patient's medical history.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This will enable practitioners to make better care decisions for their patients.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We have integrated the HealthHub application within the NEHR.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In addition to viewing health information, such as drug allergies and medications, patients and their authorised caregivers can also manage their medical appointments via the HealthHub app.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: With Healthy 365, patients can check their health points, track their physical activities and diet as well as access community activities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We intend to progressively make available more health information from the NEHR on the HealthHub app.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We are also exploring how to better facilitate the sharing of health and administrative data between these partners.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The sharing of data also enables public agencies such as the HPB and Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) to formulate national programmes, initiate new preventive healthcare programmes or reach out to residents who may be socially isolated and require support.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: For example, through its Preventive Health Visits with seniors, AIC's SGO shares relevant information it gathers with AACs and the Regional Health Systems so that they can follow up with relevant programmes for their residents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This was announced by Minister Ong Ye Kung during the COS debate last year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: There are three things the legislation will seek to achieve.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Given the sensitive nature of health information and the consequences of misuse, stringent requirements must be placed on the collection, use and sharing of health information.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: There are measures already in place under the Personal Data Protection Act and the Cybersecurity Act, and these requirements already apply to our healthcare providers today.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We are engaging the Personal Data Protection Commission (PDPC) and the Cyber Security Agency of Singapore (CSA) to identify areas where requirements need to be strengthened and where safeguards need to be fortified, specifically for health information.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Health information is personal and it is something that Singaporeans expect to be carefully and sensitively handled.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Thus, beyond engaging the PDPC and CSA, we have been extensively consulting stakeholders on issues surrounding data privacy and sharing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These include our licensees, healthcare professionals, IT vendors, members of the public, patients and caregivers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The views gathered are helping us shape the Bill to address our policy intent, the needs of patients and the administrative and operational costs for providers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: If I may, Sir, turn to addressing some of the cuts that Members have filed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Alex Yam asked if the gestation limit for abortion could be lowered.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Many countries have similar rules as us and allow for abortions for medical and socioeconomic reasons after 20 weeks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: At 23 weeks gestation, there are high risks that these extremely pre-term babies if they survive, lead a very poor quality of life.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Although it is improving, the chance of survival remains low.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We will continue to work with the professional community to monitor the neonatal survival and morbidity data, and continue to evaluate the appropriate gestational threshold.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Nonetheless, we are aware that the success rates of egg freezing remain relatively stable up to 37 years old at the point of donation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We are reviewing the evidence as part of the overall effort in developing the Assisted Reproduction Regulations under the HCSA.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We agree with Dr Tan that we need to sustain our efforts on the affordability of cancer treatment while keeping MediShield Life premiums affordable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Over the five-year period from 2017 to 2021, this spending increased by over 90% while overall national age-adjusted cancer mortality improved by 2.1%.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The CDL has allowed MOH to negotiate for lower drug prices, thus making cancer treatments more cost-effective and lowering the financial burden on patients and families.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Expensive and novel treatments may not equate to better outcomes, and we strongly encourage patients and practitioners to choose the listed drugs where possible.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: A minority of patients are on non-CDL treatments and they may need time to adjust to the changes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Multiple support measures are being provided to help them continue with their current treatment course with minimal impact to their out-of-pocket expenses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These include financial support for existing patients in our public institutions and the preservation of IPs coverage until 30 September this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Thereafter, non-CDL treatments may remain covered by private insurance products, such as IP riders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: If affordability is an issue in private healthcare institutions, patients can opt for subsidised care at the public healthcare institutions where they may apply for additional support such as MediFund.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Patients who receive ancillary services such as consultations, scans and blood tests as part of their cancer drug treatment and those requiring more intensive treatments are worried about future treatment costs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These can be claimed from MediShield Life under a separate cancer drug services limit.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: As such, they are not allowed to provide any licensable healthcare services or purport to treat, diagnose or manage any medical conditions or diseases.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We do not allow unlicensed providers to advertise services or skills relating to the treatment of a medical condition.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These measures will be ported over to the Healthcare Services (Amendment) Bill, which will be debated in the House later this month.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This allows unlicensed providers to be subject to the same penalties as licensed providers, if they contravene the regulations on healthcare advertising under the HCSA.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We take a serious view of this and will not hesitate to take errant providers to task.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Members of the public are encouraged to remain wary of exaggerated claims when consuming healthcare services from unlicensed providers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: I also agree with Dr Tan that the CCRP could be used more widely.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It was designed to be voluntary, where parties using the CCRP must mutually agree to participate and abide by the CCRP's decision via a contract.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: MOH will continue to work with the relevant organisations to strengthen the CCRP process and its participation by all stakeholders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: To Dr Tan's suggestion of a future collaboration with SMA in enhancing the education of payers, we agree that stronger collaboration between payers and the care team will contribute to a better patient experience, and this can be discussed further with the MHIC.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: MOH currently requires licensees using third party administrator (TPA) services to reflect TPA administrative fees in the patient's bill.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: However, as there is no direct patient care involved, we do not regulate the TPAs themselves.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We understand that there are concerns about the potential impact on healthcare affordability and access when using TPAs, and we remain committed to minimising the risks by working closely with stakeholders, such as the College of Family Physicians.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In response to Dr Shahira Abdullah, our two NSCs, namely the NUCOHS and the NDCS were set up to provide subsidised dental services for patients requiring more complex or specialist dental treatment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Although the NSCs also receive subsidised patient referrals directly from other Government hospitals, these numbers are very small and there is adequate capacity at the two NSCs to manage referrals for specialist treatment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: On special care and geriatric dentistry, the Bachelor of Dental Surgery programme at the NUS includes training in geriatric dentistry.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Today, the majority of dental needs of geriatric or special needs patients are met by general dentists.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We are reviewing and monitoring dental specialities that are not formally recognised by the Dental Specialist Accreditation Board in Singapore, including the need for clinical practice guidelines for geriatric and special needs dentistry.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Beyond these measures, healthcare institutions are provided funding to enable better accessibility and care transition for elderly and special needs patients, and we encourage dentists to tap on the institutional scholarships or the Health Manpower Development Plan to pursue further clinical training in these areas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Pritam Singh wishes to understand more about the VIFAP for COVID-19 vaccination.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
