text: To determine eligibility for VIFAP, the panel reviews the medical details of the application objectively alongside available scientific evidence, to assess if it was likely caused by the COVID-19 vaccine received and its severity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It is not necessary to prove absolute causality for a payout to be awarded.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This is in line with the standards applied internationally and by the World Health Organization.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Payouts for events assessed to be related to the vaccine are based on the panel's assessment of severity, including if activities of daily living are affected.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Persons will also continue to receive support through applicable healthcare financing schemes, such as CareShield Life, MediShield Life and subsidies at our public healthcare institutions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Unsuccessful applicants can file an application for reassessment if new evidence becomes available.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We have informed healthcare professionals to be facilitative and support their patient's applications in a timely manner.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: That said, I would like to assure the House that patients have three years to apply for VIFAP.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: With time, if new evidence emerges showing potential links between vaccination and a severe adverse event, the VIFAP panel may reassess related applications.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Chairman, Sir, if I may now shift the focus to mental health.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We recognise the multifaceted nature of mental health issues and the need for better coordination between the health and social sectors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: For this reason, the Interagency Task Force on Mental Health and Well-being was established in July 2021 to oversee and coordinate mental health efforts across different sectors, focusing on cross-cutting issues that require interagency collaborations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The task force is co-led by MOH and MSF and comprises public sector agencies, such as the MCCY, MOE and MOM, as well as private and people sector agencies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Dr Wan Rizal and Mr Xie Yao Quan have asked for an update on the work done and plans under the task force.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In the past year, members of the task force played an important role in reviewing the population's mental health needs, identifying gaps and challenges and developing plans for improvements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: To gather views and feedback on the preliminary recommendations, the task force conducted public consultations between May and August 2022.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In general, respondents agreed with and were supportive of the preliminary recommendations, and most of the feedback were suggestions to refine the implementation details.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: If I may, let me now elaborate on some of the plans under the task force.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We have recommended to implement a tiered care model for mental healthcare delivery.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This is a framework that matches the level of care to the severity of the mental health needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The model is based on the idea that different individuals have different levels of mental health needs at different times and interventions can be tailored to meet each person's specific needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The tiers differ in their levels of care intensity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: For instance, the first tier typically involves self-help resources, peer support networks and hotlines offering basic emotional support for individuals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Individuals with more severe mental health symptoms would access higher level of care, such as ones involving psychotherapy or more intensive medical treatment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: What are the benefits of this model and how is it different from the existing model of service delivery?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The tiered care model will map both health and social services involved in mental healthcare delivery into the same framework, using the same language and mental models.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This will facilitate clearer referrals, coordination and care planning for individuals whose needs are managed by different service providers who may be operating from the social, educational and clinical care sectors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Last year, KKH embarked on Temasek Foundation Youth Connect pilot programme to support adolescents facing difficulties with life challenges or mental health issues.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The multidisciplinary KKH team came together with counsellors and social workers from schools and social service agencies to develop a set of intervention resources.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: KKH is also working closely with schools and community providers to facilitate referrals of adolescent patients between social services and healthcare settings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Such collaborations ensure that adolescents' needs are holistically met through the respective touchpoints.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Another example from social and education stakeholders – recognising the need for deeper collaboration to meet the mental health and well-being needs of students, AMKFSC Community Services has been working closely with counsellors from Nanyang Polytechnic (NYP) to ensure timely and coordinated mental health support for students facing academic stress as well as family and peer relationship issues.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Other benefits of the tiered care model include ensuring better access to care and encouraging early help-seeking and intervention.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The mapping of services and professionals across the tiers in the care model serves as a signpost to the public on the mental health resources and touchpoints available in the community, primary and tertiary care settings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This supports individuals in identifying the services that best meets their needs and gives them the know-how to access care as early as possible.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Ultimately, the goal of the model is to ensure individuals receive the care most appropriate for their needs in a timely manner.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In doing so, it also avoids an overreliance on centralised specialist care and optimises the use of resources.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: For the tiered care model to be implemented effectively, there is a need to ensure adequate competencies and standards amongst all mental health practitioners.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The framework will spell out the training needs of the practitioners and, through this, mental health training courses can be aligned towards a common set of training standards as described by the framework.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The framework will apply to practitioners involved in supporting individuals with mental health needs, ranging from lay responders, such as peer supporters, to mental health professionals, including nurses, social workers and counsellors, amongst others.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Practitioners can benefit by receiving more consistent and evidence-based instruction and training.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This uplifts mental health care capabilities for all providers, which will result in higher quality care and improved outcomes for clients.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: That is why HPB launched the "It's OKAY to Reach Out" campaign, to emphasise that help-seeking is appropriate and to encourage individuals to seek help for their mental health needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Normalising conversations on mental health will take time and may require different approaches for different citizen segments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: At the broad level, we continue to encourage such conversations through the SG Mental Well-being Network.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: To better support parents, HPB rolled out a public education campaign for parents to better understand their children's emotional health and identify behaviours of concern, so that parents can be better equipped to support their children and know where to seek help from as early as possible.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The Interagency Task Force fulfils the critical role of bringing together diverse partners and stakeholders to shape mental health policies and strategies, spearhead initiatives, proliferate resources and create a conducive environment for ground-up initiatives to thrive.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: With these efforts, we can expect a cohesive system of diverse mental health service providers coordinating care within a common frame of reference and a tiered model of care delivery.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: A more well-defined competency training framework will enhance the quality of care provided to all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: And I hope we will develop a more inclusive and supportive culture as a nation, with improved awareness and knowledge on mental health and well-being.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: As we emerge from the pandemic, I would like to express my deepest gratitude once again to the healthcare workers who have held the fort and led us through the pandemic.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: With that, Sir, I wish you and all Singaporeans good health.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mr Chairman, my colleagues have spoken at length about the upcoming initiatives in healthcare.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In order for those to bear fruit, it is essential that we grow and retain our healthcare workforce.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We often say that healthcare workers are the backbone or the lifeblood of the healthcare sector.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: These medical metaphors are correct because if the healthcare system were a body, none of it would function without healthcare workers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: It is, therefore, important that we continue to recruit healthcare workers from diverse sources and ensure that the sector remains an attractive one.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Our manpower policies are designed to meet present and future needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We regularly update our projections to ensure that we plan this well.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We have increased local intakes of students over time to ensure a stable supply of healthcare professionals.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This increase will materialise in the workforce in the coming years.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: As the demand for healthcare services grows and our care model evolves, we will continue to work with schools to review our intakes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We want to attract students from all pathways into suitable healthcare programmes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Take, for example, the Diploma in Nursing offered by polytechnics.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Besides "N" Level, "O" Level and "A" Level pathways, students can also join from the Integrated and International Baccalaureate Programmes, whether at the fourth or sixth year of study.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The other nursing schools like ITE and NUS also offer multiple admission pathways.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We are working towards making the entry criteria for each pathway more transparent.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: I want to assure all students that while there are entry criteria, no student from any particular educational pathway is denied eligibility.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Healthcare staff are also encouraged to continue upgrading their skills and practise at the top of their licence.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Our nurses, pharmacists and allied health professionals work closely with doctors to step up to lead care initiatives in the community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: By expanding and advancing their skillset, they can look forward to a long and fulfilling career in healthcare.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: However, the most important and urgent step we need to take is to beef up nursing manpower.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In recent years, the global competition for healthcare workers has intensified, especially for nurses.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The loss of both local and foreign nurses to our competitor countries is a key reason for the stress and high workload for our nurses.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We need to replace the manpower lost to other countries, safeguard the welfare of nurses and meet increasing needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Therefore, as Ms Mariam Jaafar has rightly pointed out, the most critical and practical thing to do is to increase manpower.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: To this end, we are ramping up recruitment of foreign nurses.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We will go through a period of increased inflow of foreign nurses because of their higher attrition in recent years.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Looking forward, we will continue to need foreign nurses to complement our local core.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Because if our population has more and more seniors and fewer young graduates joining the workforce, the numbers will not add up and local nurses alone cannot meet our healthcare needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We are glad that Members share these concerns, such as Ms Sylvia Lim, who asked about our measures to retain experienced foreign staff.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Some of these foreign healthcare workers may grow to become valued members of our healthcare community and demonstrate their commitment to Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We should be prepared to grant them PR status, because it means retaining a pool of manpower that is of critical value to Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: So, I hope all Members of this House will support our efforts to expand the manpower of the healthcare sector, including recruitment of foreign manpower.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This allows us to deliver quality healthcare and safeguard the welfare of our healthcare workers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: After recruiting them, it is equally important that we retain the healthcare workers we have.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: To answer Mr Gerald Giam's question, we review salaries regularly to ensure that healthcare workers are paid competitively.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Last year, we announced an enhanced special payment package for nurses in both the public and community care sectors.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Among the public healthcare institutions, they will also refresh and update pay components, such as allowances for shifts and for work duties beyond regular hours.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: As Dr Tan Wu Meng has pointed out, other measures, such as flexible work arrangements can help retain staff who might leave otherwise.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: For those who leave the sector, our healthcare institutions maintain contact to encourage them to return.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We will continue with our efforts to retain the nursing workforce.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Last but certainly not least, we will continue to ensure the well-being of our healthcare workers and that starts with a healthy working culture and environment.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Those who have worked in a healthcare institution will know that many of our healthcare workers work beyond their call of duty, skip meals and forego rest time.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Their strong sense of duty keeps them going, but it is neither sustainable nor fair that they constantly sacrifice their well-being.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In a profession where people come first, there must be more we can do to ensure their welfare.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We work closely with public healthcare clusters on this.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The clusters also regularly survey staff on whether they feel able to cope with the demands at work and whether they know how to seek help when faced with stress or workplace bullying.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: At present, the hospitals use methods like electronic logging and surveys to monitor junior doctors' working hours and well-beings.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: That said, hospitals are operational environments which have to address patient needs on a day-to-day basis.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: When planning rosters, hospitals take into account the skill mix of staff on each shift and each staff's preferred shift pattern.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Healthcare workers have also covered for each other occasionally where there is an operational need.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In addition, Singaporeans can show their support by lightening the load on healthcare workers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Each of us can avoid bogging nurses down with administrative and basic tasks that do not require nursing expertise to address.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Family members can do their part in assisting their loved ones in the hospitals with basic care, such as feeding and moving around.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: It is also reassuring for patients to be attended to by their loved ones.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Your support in such activities will allow nurses to focus on complex care tasks, such as medication administration and wound care.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We are grateful to those who already do their best to support healthcare workers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Last year, the Ministry announced that we were forming a Tripartite Workgroup to look into the rising number of cases where healthcare workers had been abused and harassed.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Since then, we have extensively engaged healthcare workers and members of the public on this issue.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Based on our findings, abuse has become a more common occurrence that healthcare workers face.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We need to have a clear and common definition of abuse across healthcare workers and members of the public.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: It also means taking steps to prevent potentially abusive situations, as well as promoting trust and respect between patients, caregivers and healthcare workers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We appreciate that Members of this House have raised various questions on this important issue.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: As shared by Minister Ong earlier, we have completed the first phase of our work.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We will share more details of the Workgroup's engagement findings and a progress update on MOH's plans later this month.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Last year, I spoke about our efforts to reach out to ethnic minority groups, including the formation of the Malay Community Outreach, or MCO, Workgroup.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: I also shared on HPB's efforts to use culturally significant events for public education on healthier lifestyles.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We have kept up the momentum of these efforts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: To engage the Indian community, we promoted healthy eating messages during Deepavali, such as the need to reduce sugar consumption in desserts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The public may have seen last year's Deepavali music video with Mediacorp's Vasantham.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: HPB also held exercise sessions and health screenings in places of worship, such as the Central Sikh Temple.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mr Chairman, please allow me to say a few words in Malay.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: (In Malay):   To encourage people to take charge of their own health, we are making it easier for the community to organise and run their own programmes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: One example is a new initiative by the MCO Workgroup, called Saham Kesihatan (Healthy Investment), which was piloted at M3@Towns at Tampines and Jurong.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: It is aimed at nurturing a group of peer leaders in the community who organise community-led interest groups for Malay/Muslim residents to live healthily.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: For people who lead sedentary lifestyles, it can feel challenging to get into the habit of exercising.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Luckily, it is never too late to start.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Someone who illustrates that perfectly is Mdm Haslina Aziz, who is an active volunteer and leader in Gems Empowering Me Series.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Gems is a social enterprise that organises activities for women to lead healthy lifestyles.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Since joining Gems almost 10 years ago, Mdm Haslina has participated in activities such as Spartan Races, sea expeditions and dragon boating.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This is a woman at the peak of her physical prowess, and you might assume I am describing someone in her 20s.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In fact, Mdm Haslina is a grandmother of five.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: She has diabetes but keeps that in check by making a sustained effort to live healthily.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: She shows us that age and medical conditions should not deter us from pursuing an active lifestyle.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We often think that participating in sports activities helps to keep us active and healthy.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Let us think of it this way instead: it is by staying active and healthy that we are able to continue enjoying these activities well into our golden years.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: And that is what makes for a fulfilling life.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: On that note, I encourage everyone to join us at the Saham Kesihatan Family Festival at Our Tampines Hub next Sunday morning on 12 March.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We will be starting at 8.30am with a mass workout, followed by a team telematch with quizzes and physical activities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Afterwards, you can explore the festival to learn about nutrition and health screening.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: There is also a health zone where residents can learn about the importance of quitting smoking and HPB's "I Quit" programme.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: If anyone in your family is a smoker, please take this chance to speak to them seriously about quitting smoking.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We all have a part to play in nudging family and friends towards adopting a healthy lifestyle.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This extends to the Malay/Muslim community as well.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: If you have a passion for organising healthy lifestyle activities for our community, the carnival will have booths where you can sign up with our M3@ Towns partners.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This is a fun opportunity for the community to get together and make the switch to a healthy lifestyle.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: (In English): Mr Chairman, as we embark on the Healthier SG strategy, the public can expect to see more of such programmes for ethnic minority groups, as well as for the rest of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: As Mr Xie Yao Quan has pointed out, it is important that we make it easy to join these activities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: HPB conducts physical activity programmes, such as weekly exercise sessions and these are accessible, regardless of which neighbourhood you live in.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: You can sign up conveniently through the Healthy 365 app.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Seniors who are unfamiliar with a smartphone can ask their relatives to sign up on their behalf, or simply walk in with their identity card.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Community involvement is key to ensuring that health promotion efforts are sustained for the long term.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We believe in supporting and encouraging more ground-up initiatives to meet the needs of the community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We are heartened by how these Singaporeans have dedicated their time and skills to improve the health of their community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Small lifestyle changes can go a long way towards lasting habits and better health outcomes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This is especially true for those with chronic medical conditions like diabetes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: To provide diabetes patients with health information to manage their condition, we worked with more than 40 expert members and patient champions to develop Tier 2 of the National Diabetes Reference Materials.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: It will contain easy-to-understand information on diabetic care, like reading nutrition labels and monitoring glycaemic index.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We hope that this will empower diabetic patients and their caregivers to "be aware, be healthy and be proactive" to manage and live with diabetes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: As we talk about healthy lifestyles, a major area of concern is smoking.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Tobacco use is the single greatest cause of preventable death globally.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: To answer Mr Ang Wei Neng's question on anti-vaping measures, we take a multi-pronged approach to address the issue of vaping, including enforcement and education measures.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: At Singapore's borders, the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority works with the HSA for detection and enforcement of illegal imports of e-vaporisers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: HSA monitors and targets the illicit sales of e-vaporisers on social media and messaging platforms to curb online access.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: HSA and the National Environment Agency (NEA) are working together on a cross-enforcement pilot for NEA's enforcement officers to also act against vaping offences.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Lastly, HPB has rolled out a digital campaign to raise awareness on the illegality and negative health effects of vaping, as well as how it leads to nicotine addiction.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In schools, we are raising awareness among students about the benefits of leading a nicotine-free lifestyle.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: When students are caught using or possessing e-vaporisers, it will be confiscated and their parents will be informed.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: School-based disciplinary action is taken, including suspension, or caning for boys.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: They are referred to counsellors who will guide them through their cessation journey to effect long-term behavioural change.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Recalcitrant offenders may be referred to HSA which may issue them a fine.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Youths might also have misconceptions about smoking and vaping.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: It is important that we dispel these misconceptions and equip youths with knowledge and life skills to say no to cigarettes and e-vaporisers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Parents have a part to play as well, and they can refer to relevant information and resources through online articles on Parent Hub.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Preventive health forms the foundation for better health.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We are heartened that many have participated in our programmes and made a lasting switch to a healthy lifestyle.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: But we must be self-motivated in order to sustain these lifestyle changes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Singaporeans have it within them to take charge of their health and to create the health outcomes they want to have.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
text: Chairman, I thank Dr Janil for the detailed replies.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
text: Regarding wellness and beauty salons claiming to offer treatments for slimming and detox, such as fat loss pills and lymphatic treatments to reduce cancer risk: firstly, are these medical treatments?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: If they are unlicensed providers, we can take them to task.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I encourage the Member or members of the public to notify us directly if they come across such an instance and make a complaint.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Ultimately, perhaps one of the best ways to protect themselves is to have a regular relationship with a trusted care provider.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
text: So, the three questions I had were: are these considered medical treatment; how do we recognise misleading claims; and who do we report to?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: On Dr Tan's second question of how to recognise the misleading claims, I think this is an area where there is quite a lot of education that is needed.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, I think the first thing is to establish whether this is a licensed medical provider.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: The first one is on the good news of normalising telehealth.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: I am very glad to hear the response to my cut that the time limited extension of telehealth for CHAS subsidies and MediSave to be applicable for chronic disease management is going to come.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: But in the time extension, it was specified for video consultation.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: So, my clarification is for proven health technology – such as the class of remote vital signs monitoring technology, which has been proven effective for hypertension management, for example, in the United States as well as in pilots in Singapore – will they be considered?

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: The second question I have is on the AACs.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: I cannot agree with the Minister more that community nodes like these are extremely important to motivate our seniors, especially to live actively and maintain their health.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: I want to ask how fast would the expansion plan be.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: I have two sites in my constituency that has no AAC.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: We have willing partners who are very keen to start.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But if it involves consultation, whether by phone, by video, these are efficacious interventions and they should be covered.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: What we want is to bring telehealth in, to normalise the funding and support for telehealth, but there is a range of practices.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Dr Tan Yia Swam also mentioned there are so many different kinds; and some will claim to be efficacious, but they are not.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, I think we also need a gateway system to make sure that the legitimate ones, useful ones, we support; but keeping out the not useful or even detrimental ones.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: On the expansion of AACs, we are on the same page.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We want to expand quickly as we can.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I mentioned and I have alluded to the possibility that this may become a significant national programme.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As I mentioned, we are racing against time.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: In the community, we can see in a matter of months, how some of our residents become frail.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: They do need the support near their homes, in the neighbourhoods, to keep them active, healthy, give them friends.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, I hope I can give an update very soon.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: According to the AIC website, the household monthly income per person ceiling for the HCG is $2,800.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: But according to the Department of Statistics (DOS), the median monthly household income from work per household member in 2022 was $3,287.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: So, should the HCG not be using the $3,287 number instead of $2,800?

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: We have the recognition that ageing is going at a relentless pace and I am quite taken aback by the numbers of how many healthcare workers we need.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: Last year, I spoke about incorporating or rather setting up a care force as part of "national service" so that our young men and women can be tapped on to help with healthcare manpower needs.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: Is there any possibility that the Ministry might look into this as a model that could help us with this very urgent care avalanche that simply just needs more hands on deck?

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: I understand there are many functions within a healthcare system that do not require medical training and can relieve a lot of the nurses' workload.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I am sorry, I do not recall the care force proposal.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: If it is meant to be some form of "national service" for women, I think you need to pose this to the Ministry of Defence.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: For MOH, if we really expand AACs into a ubiquitous support system for our aged and seniors and to be able to befriend them, engage them in activities, teach them digital literacy, teach them how to use HealthHub, how to use Healthy 365, monitor their vital signs, I think we need a lot of volunteers, just befriending.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: In my own constituency, we are trying very hard to recruit such a care force.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: You do not require a lot of medical training.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: In fact, you require a lot of heart and to be able to commit a morning every month during the weekend – every week is better – and just have enough hands and legs; and I think we can do a lot more for our seniors in the community.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah
text: Previously, Khoo Teck Puat Hospital's dental clinic already offers the full range of subsidised specialised treatment for many, many years.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah
text: But now, for the treatment to be subsidised, the hospital needs to partner with an NSC.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah
text: So, they actually do have the capacity and capability.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah
text: For example, if you want to go from a Registrar to an Associate Consultant (AC), you cannot because there is no board exam to pass.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah
text: I understand that MOH will be doing a review, but for the time being, will MOH consider coming out with a set career progression ladder for them, especially in hospitals?

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah
text: Because I think it will really encourage people to go into this field.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We will look at the career progression issue, but we also do need to make sure that where there is this process of specialist accreditation and career progression, we do give a structure that provides assurance to the practitioner as they progress along their career, to the institution that employs him or her, and to the patients.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I think we do want to wait for that process to work through as we review the needs and the process of doing specialist accreditation within dentistry.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: On the issue of subsidised treatments, the bottom line is that there are very few patients that require that type of treatment outside of the NSCs.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The NSCs continue to have quite a lot of capacity.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We would like for these treatments to be provided where there is a significant patient load and significant service provider experience as well.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Currently, they are concentrated at the national centres.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Could I just ask, what else are we doing further?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I know we are ramping up the hiring of more nurses, but that could be just replacing the nurses who are resigning; and we are in this vicious cycle.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: In all the dialogues with nurses, there is this a recurring cry for help and fatigue.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: It is really not like a two-day vacation to rest and recharge but, really, they are burning out.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I fear that we will lose more instead of being able to hire more.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Again, that is the vicious cycle that we are in now.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I would say, particularly, Members of Parliament such as Mr Ng who come into contact with healthcare workers, you would hear a lot more feedback that is more stark.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I think the pandemic has something to do with it.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: In these three years, really, the workload has been relentless.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: In terms of attrition, I should correct some misperception that we are losing doctors, that we are losing local nurses.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: That is because many countries were desperate for nurses and we lost foreign nurses because of that.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, in hospitals, in certain wards and the emergency departments, these are sometimes shorthanded – the answer is yes.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As I mentioned, this is the main issue.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We can set rest days, enforce rest time and all that, but we know our nurses.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: When there are patients, they will take care of them, even though it is their rest time.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I think the best way to support them would be to beef up the manpower.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: If you plot and interpolate the numbers, in between, we do need to expand the manpower.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: In terms of local recruitment, Senior Parliamentary Secretary Rahayu has mentioned a lot of things we are doing.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I should say healthcare is an attractive sector for many young people.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, it is not a sector which people are avoiding.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: If you look at 20 students, I know one is joining MOH and our healthcare system.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I do not want to describe in too much details what are the techniques that we are using, but I think Singapore is a fairly attractive place to many nurses out there.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Similarly, as it is attractive to many of our young students, they want to join healthcare.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I think what the attraction is: we are a safe city to live in and in joining our system, there is a career pathway and there is very good training.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: By and large, except for the very small minority, it is a well-respected profession.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: So, if they are compliant to whatever social prescription that is given by their GP, what is the reward system going to be given to them?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: Lastly, on the Healthy 365 app, currently, how many Singaporeans are actually on this particular app?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: It seems that the Ministry is going to push the main platform for Healthier SG through HealthHub as well as Healthy 365.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Second, is the reward system after the sign-up.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Because when it comes to preventive care, you cannot run away from exercise and taking steps, keeping your heartbeat moderate to intense certain times of a week and, therefore, Healthy 365 is one way to keep you going.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Yes, keep on reminding you that you can accumulate health points by having an active lifestyle.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, this is the reward system that is long-lasting.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: How to get more people onto Healthy 365?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I think your neighbour has a very good suggestion – to hold carnivals.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The Member mentioned the two apps – one is Health Hub; and the other is Healthy 365.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I just want to explain that we need both apps.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I know there was a suggestion to lump everything into one app.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But I think we have so many apps in our smartphone, we can live with two.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: These are data that can be shared across healthcare providers in different settings.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: You can show your doctor, but this is actually your data, it will not be shared.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: As part of our plans to improve palliative and end-of-life care, how will the Government promote the use and awareness of the My Legacy portal?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: There is a lot of useful information and services inside, such as applying for your LPA as well as ACP.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: I can say that many residents on the ground do not know about this and it is useful for them to get more awareness about this.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: Second, just now, the Minister mentioned that a lot of volunteers are needed for the AACs.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: Will MOH consider creating micro jobs for seniors to take up some of these tasks, like befriending other seniors and escort services for medical appointments?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: These will also keep them active and healthy in the spirit of Healthier SG.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But on an issue as personal as how you decide you want to go and where you want to go, it goes beyond a portal that we actually need to consciously speak to patients and their loved ones about, and have that conversation early on.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: You never know, with Healthier SG, once you develop a long-term, patient-doctor relationship with a trusted doctor, at some point, it is something that the doctor can speak to you about.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And once you think about it, these are things you may have to even discuss within the family and, in that context, then refer to My Legacy portal.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: This is how I think it will work.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: It is quite unlikely that you are surfing the Internet, ChatGPT – how should I go – and suddenly come upon a revelation, it is quite unlikely.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: It requires quite a serious intimate discussion with somebody you trust.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Many of our AACs actually look into that.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: They do have one word of caution – that you do not want to pay your volunteers just cash.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: In fact, for many seniors, it is not about the payment but about getting involved, feeling useful and then being recognised in some way.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: It could be health points or could be something else.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: I have a question on the training framework he mentioned earlier.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: Can I get clarifications on whether there is a regulatory body to manage the trained personnel that he mentioned earlier?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: I ask because I understand that there will be peer leaders that will be involved, and I know that, being peer leaders on the ground, there will be many and there is a need for us to recognise that we want to keep these standards high, especially when it comes to mental health issues although it is the early stages.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: I am not sure the Minister addressed my question about creating more temporary nursing home places for respite care.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: This is something that quite a few of my residents have requested.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We have to expand the capabilities as well as capacities and, where they are available.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We will make it available, and we are working with AIC to do so.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Dr Tan Wu Meng, would you like to withdraw your amendment, please?

text: (In Mandarin):   I would like to thank our frontline workers, healthcare providers and public officers.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Because of your contribution and sacrifice, we can finally reopen and see the sunshine again!

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: (In Malay):   As a community that helps one another, as a community that is united, as friends of different races, languages and religions, we were able to overcome the COVID-19 pandemic!

speaker: The Chairman
text: Dr Tan, when you ask for my indulgence, I did not realise you were going for all the different languages.
